text:
maria: Heads-up — customer doing private deploy wants us to prove isolation guarantees for on‑prem. Questions about KMS integration, audit log streaming, and strict egress/netpols. Can we sketch a minimal gated architecture and short checklist?

raj: 👍 quick Qs: are they using AWS KMS via a VPC endpoint, Vault HSM, or a totally air-gapped HSM?

maria: They said air‑gapped colo for data-plane, but control-plane can talk out over a managed tunnel to our control plane. KMS will be on their side (Vault + HSM) — we need to support customer-managed key workflows and key wrap/unwrapped TBs.

alex: For RBAC, we should push least privilege: separate service identities for "control-plane" vs "runtime". Runtime only needs Encrypt/Decrypt for inference keys, no key create/delete. Control-plane gets key management roles.

sophia: Also add ephemeral credentials and short TTLs. Our agent should call the customer's KMS via a short-lived cert issued by their CA. No long-lived static keys on disk.

sec-bot: Note: previous private deploy (INC-2024-72) failed audit because audit logs were buffered locally without integrity markers. Add hashed chaining and remote-forwarding requirement.

maria: Good call. For audit streaming we propose Fluentd -> TLS -> customer Splunk/ELK over the same managed tunnel. Must sign/sequence events and include request IDs and model id + version.

raj: For network isolation, recommended pattern: control-plane <-> management tunnel (mutual TLS), nodes have no direct internet egress except to the customer's jump-proxy. Enforce via k8s NetworkPolicy + host firewall.

alex: Example minimal NetworkPolicy we discussed:

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-except-proxy
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.0.0/24  # customer's proxy/jump host
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

sophia: Add host-level iptables to block all non-proxy egress as defense-in-depth. Also enable conntrack limits and log drops to a local tamper-evident store.

maria: Regarding KMS calls: we need to ensure token binding so that even if a runtime cert is stolen it can't be used elsewhere. Recommend mTLS with client cert + TPM attestation (if available).

raj: For RBAC change workflow: PR in infra repo -> automated policy test that simulates impersonation -> require 2 approvers from security + infra. Rollout via canary to 1 cluster. Revert window 30m.

ops-oncall: On incidents, require immediate key-use audit: list of decrypt operations in last 15m + pod/host identity. We need a quick script that queries both KMS audit and our request-trace index. I can add a runbook entry.

maria: Action items: 1) alex to draft NetworkPolicy + iptables snippet; 2) sophia to write ephemeral cert flow & attestation options; 3) raj to draft RBAC PR template and test harness; 4) ops-oncall to add incident playbook entry. Deliverables by EOW?

alex: I can post a short PR with the NetworkPolicy + `iptables` snippet by Thursday.

sophia: I'll prototype a cert issuance flow that uses the customer's CA and TPM attest statements — ETA Friday.

raj: I'll sketch the RBAC PR template and add an automated impersonation test in CI — aiming EOW.

ops-oncall: I'll add the key‑use audit script into runbooks repo and wire up a Slack alert that posts basic summary to #incidents.

maria: One more compliance nicety: add integrity markers on audit batches (HMAC with a rotation key stored in their Vault) so they can detect tampering during transport.

sec-bot: Scan results: a dependency (fluentd-plugin-http) flagged CVE-2025-xxxx — prefer using our maintained forwarder container.

maria: Noted — we'll avoid that plugin and use the vetted forwarder. Thanks all. I'll consolidate notes into a short PR describing the architecture and checklist.

raj: If anyone wants to pair on the impersonation test I can schedule 30m after lunch.

alex: ping me, I'll join.

sophia: +1

maria: Closing out — I'll create the PR and link the runbook updates. :thumbsup:
